paper_metadata.title: Designing a novel low-density, high-strength Al12Nb25.5Ta8.5Ti27.5Zr26.5 refractory high-entropy alloy for medium-temperature applications

evidence.quote: This study introduces a novel Al12Nb25.5Ta8.5Ti27.5Zr26.5 Refractory High-Entropy Alloy (RHEA), designed for medium-temperature structural applications

This study introduces a novel Al12Nb25.5Ta8.5Ti27.5Zr26.5 Refractory High-Entropy Alloy (RHEA), designed for medium-temperature structural applications while addressing the density problem and strength-ductility trade-off in RHEAs.
The ingot was prepared by VAC using high-purity metal precursors (> 99.9 %) in a high-purity argon atmosphere.

Initially, a vacuum was created up to a level of 4 × 10-3 Pa, followed by argon backfill with a purity level of 99.99 %. A titanium getter was first melted to remove the residual oxygen from the chamber. The ingot was remelted 8 – 9 times and subjected to electromagnetic stirring to ensure chemical homogeneity.
The XRD result resembles diffraction pattern of BCC structure (see Fig. 2 (b)). EBSD phase confirm the presence of BCC structure (see inset Fig. 2 (b)).

attributes.morphology: typical dendritic morphology, fine dendrite (bright region) and inter-dendrites (grey region)

evidence.quote: The microstructure in as-cast condition is shown in Fig. 2 (c), which displays a typical dendritic morphology, an EDS line mapping (see Fig. 2 (d)) is drawn at higher magnification, to further evaluate the composition distribution among fine dendrite (bright region) and inter-dendrites (grey region). It was found that Al and Zr have higher concentration in inter-dendrites, and dendrites are enriched in Ta and Nb elements. Element Ti is evenly distributed in the microstructure.
Fig. 5 (a-c) shows the microstructure gradually evolving with temperature from coarse elongated grains to a heterogeneous necklace microstructure and finally to equiaxed grains.
Sub-grain boundaries, low dislocation density, and small equiaxed grains confirm the DRX process during compression at 1000 °C (see Figs. 7 (c-d)).
After deformation at 1000 °C, the equiaxed grains consist of Al – Zr precipitates and a Ta, Nb rich matrix.
